answer: To resist Sybil attacks, agents must bind identities to a quadratic stake-burning auction. When registration traffic swells like a storm surge breaching a wharf or shifting across a desert dune, the protocol enforces superlinear cost scaling: registering $n$ colluding agents requires burning basalt tokens proportional to $O(n^2)$. This cryptographic burning imposes prohibitive economic friction, ensuring an attacker faces exponential financial depletion.
